_comment: Domain rules for the architectural-memory symbol index. First match wins. Most-specific patterns first; broad catch-alls last. Domains must match /^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,49}$/.

rules._why: MUST precede the scripts/check-*.mjs catch-all (first-match-wins). That glob assigns every check-* CLI to `install`, which swallowed this one — a plan-status checker, not installation logic — and manufactured a recurring install -> plan violation out of a naming coincidence. The code was right; the map was wrong. Other check-* CLIs are likely miscategorised too (check-rls is security, check-stale-skill-surface is skills); retagged only the one with an observed violation rather than reshuffling the whole glob blind.

NARROW RULE above the scripts/check-*.mjs -> install glob, same shape and same reason as check-plan-status.mjs directly below (2026-07-17). This is a DB test-container enrolment checker, not installation logic; the glob is a naming coincidence and manufactured a recurring install -> scripts violation out of it. That rule's own note predicted this: 'Other check-* CLIs are likely miscategorised too.' Retagged when its violation was observed, still not reshuffling the glob blind. Plan: docs/plans/god-module-and-layering-debt.md group (A).

rules._comment: Phase A (domain-map-reconciliation): these subsystems each own a scripts/lib/<name>/ directory and a top-level CLI, and were silently pooled into the shared-lib catch-all below because no rule claimed them (70 of shared-lib's 156 files). shared-lib is the SECOND-TO-LAST rule — anything added under scripts/lib/ without a rule here lands in it and its deps get attributed to 'shared-lib', which is how shared-lib came to appear to import 9 feature domains. When you add a new scripts/lib/<subsystem>/, add a rule here too; tests/domain-map-dead-intent.test.mjs cannot catch this (the rule isn't dead — it's absent).

rules._why: NARROW RULE above scripts/lib/db/** -> stores. Verified at source (581fea0b): this module has ZERO imports and exports one pure classifier, normalizePostgresError, over Postgres SQLSTATE codes — no I/O, no connection, no schema knowledge. A pure error classifier is a domain-neutral primitive, not the persistence layer, and tagging it `stores` manufactured a shared-lib -> stores edge from durable-write.mjs (audit-store-write-durability decision 2c, which deliberately reuses this classifier rather than writing a second one). REFACTOR > RETAG > DECLARE: nothing to refactor here, the tag was simply wrong. Resulting stores -> shared-lib edges from the rest of lib/db/** are already declared. Plan: docs/plans/god-module-and-layering-debt.md decision 4.

RETAG, not move (domain-map-reconciliation debt entry 1, cleared 2026-08-10). These four sit at scripts/lib/ root, so the scripts/lib/** catch-all tagged them shared-lib — but they are audit COORDINATORS, not domain-neutral primitives, and each imports a feature module (efficacy-lints -> audit/, audit-shadow -> store/, finalize-outcomes -> audit/+store/, audit-arms -> model-eval/). That manufactured shared-lib -> audit-orchestration/stores/model-eval: the base layer depending UP on features, which _comment_allowedDeps recorded as debt rather than intent. The code was right; the tag was wrong — same shape as the check-plan-status rule above. Retag rather than move because their LOCATION is fine (they are top-level audit-loop modules); it is the catch-all that mis-read them. config.mjs and repo-inventory.mjs were in the same debt note and are NOT here: repo-inventory imports only shared-lib, and config.mjs is a genuine primitive whose single feature import was a trapped vocabulary constant, moved to preview-gate-vocabulary.mjs instead (REFACTOR beats RETAG when the primitive is innocent).

RETAG shared-lib, EARNED by the arm-vocabulary extraction — not a revert of d5e66d35. That commit (2026-08-10) moved this file to `model-eval` as a 'model-eval coordinator', and at the time it did import audit-orchestration: `ARM_IDS` from audit-arms.mjs. But it coordinates nothing — every export (DECISION_CONSTANTS, normalizeSeverity, sevW, qualMult, buildClusters, distinctCodeUnits, aggregateCost, evaluateDecision) is a PURE function with zero I/O, and its only feature-domain import was a frozen three-string array: a trapped vocabulary constant, the same shape as PREVIEW_GATE_MODES. Once that vocabulary moved to lib/arm-vocabulary.mjs (shared-lib), this file's imports are model-pricing.mjs + arm-vocabulary.mjs, both shared-lib. It now passes the same test d5e66d35 applied to config.mjs. ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: the extraction lands FIRST, so this retag asserts a property the code already has rather than one we wish it had. Inbound (the direction d5e66d35 forgot, verified mechanically by tests/arm-vocabulary-layering.test.mjs, not by grep): cross-skill.mjs and cross-skill/commands/model-eval.mjs are cross-skill-bridge, audit/cost-budget.mjs is audit-orchestration, dashboard/collect-telemetry.mjs is dashboard, solo-control/scoring.mjs is solo-control, plus one test — every one of those already declares shared-lib. Clears dashboard -> model-eval and solo-control -> model-eval. Plan: docs/plans/god-module-and-layering-debt.md decision 3.

RETAG, not declare (same shape as the five files d5e66d35 retagged 2026-08-10). This is the audit store's writer-registry bootstrap — audit-store-write-durability decision 1b makes it the registry's ONLY bootstrap, imported by both the orchestrator and the cross-skill CLI. It sits at scripts/lib/ root so the scripts/lib/** catch-all read it as shared-lib, and its two deliberate store imports then read as the base layer depending UP on persistence. Its LOCATION is fine; the TAG was wrong. Outbound: audit-orchestration -> stores is already declared AND observed. Inbound (the direction d5e66d35 forgot, checked mechanically by tests/arm-vocabulary-layering.test.mjs): legacy-production-audit.mjs is same-domain, cross-skill/commands/misc.mjs is cross-skill-bridge -> audit-orchestration (declared), the test file is tests -> audit-orchestration (declared). Plan: docs/plans/god-module-and-layering-debt.md decision 4.

EXPLICIT shared-lib claim, added 2026-08-13 so the domain is DECIDED rather than defaulted (audit M9, guarded by tests/domain-map-subsystem-coverage.test.mjs). Each of these six scripts/lib/<subsystem>/ directories previously reached shared-lib only via the scripts/lib/** catch-all below — the same silent default that filed scripts/lib/cross-skill/** (15 files, 4,408 lines) as shared-lib on 2026-08-12 and produced 10 layering violations including both HIGHs. VERIFIED at source before claiming, not assumed: every module in these six imports ONLY shared-lib primitives (cli-io, file-io, config, ast, path-validation, secret-patterns, azure-route-report) and no feature domain, so shared-lib is correct on the evidence and these rules change the resolved graph by ZERO edges. The point is not the domain, it is that adding a subsystem is now TWO edits — the directory and its rule — instead of one silent one. NOTE arch-memory: its files import only primitives too, so it stays shared-lib rather than moving to the same-named feature domain; retagging it would flip the `to` domain of every inbound edge (the d5e66d35 mistake) for no correctness gain.

EXPLICIT shared-lib claim, added 2026-08-14 (final-review-scoped-second-reviewer plan, Cluster A) so the domain is DECIDED rather than defaulted — same shape as the 2026-08-13 six-subsystem rule above (tests/domain-map-subsystem-coverage.test.mjs). VERIFIED at source before claiming: envelope.mjs, gap-projection.mjs and scope.mjs have ZERO import statements — pure, self-contained modules (envelope.mjs's own docstring: 'Pure: no fs, no env, no I/O'), so shared-lib is correct on the evidence, stronger than the precedent's 'shared-lib primitives only' bar. Adding the directory without this rule would have let it fall through to the scripts/lib/** catch-all silently, the same shape that produced 10 layering violations on 2026-08-12.

RETAG, finishing the job _adjudication_2026_07_31 started. That pass retagged install.mjs out of the *.mjs catch-all into `install` precisely so it would NOT have to declare tests -> root-scripts ('would have granted every test module access to the whole current and future root-scripts domain to express one narrow relationship; re-tagging removes the edge instead'). It never reached setup.mjs, its sibling installer, so tests/setup-access-routes.test.mjs -> setup.mjs survived as the last tests -> root-scripts edge. Same file class, same fix, same reason. Inbound: only that test, and tests -> install is already declared. Plan: docs/plans/god-module-and-layering-debt.md decision 4.

Catch-all for repo-root scripts, repointed root-scripts -> scripts 2026-08-12. `root-scripts` owned exactly two files: install.mjs (retagged to `install` by _adjudication_2026_07_31) and setup.mjs (retagged 2026-08-12, same reason — its sibling installer). With both gone the domain owned ZERO paths and tests/domain-map-dead-intent.test.mjs failed, correctly. The RULES are kept rather than deleted because they are a coverage net: analyseImports SKIPS an untagged file (`if (!fromDomain) continue`), so deleting the catch-all would make any future repo-root script invisible to the layering check — trading a dead domain for a blind spot. `scripts` is the other structural catch-all and docs/architecture-intent.md already groups the two together; a repo-root script is a script. tests -> scripts is already declared, so the one edge that lived here (setup-access-routes.test.mjs) stays legal.

_comment_codeless: Domains that are code-less BY DESIGN (markdown / SQL / SKILL.md-only) — they have no JS symbols, so they will never appear in the code-symbol architecture map. The Purpose-tab hygiene treats a mapped-but-no-arch domain in this list as INFORMATIONAL (a neutral note), not an actionable 'stale rule' warning. Only add a domain here once you've confirmed it genuinely has no indexable code (vs a dead/mis-targeted rule that should be fixed instead).
_comment_allowedDeps: BASELINE, NOT ENDORSEMENT (domain-map-reconciliation Phase C, 2026-07-17). Set to the OBSERVED graph AFTER Phase A fixed rule coverage (13 orphaned lib subsystems) and the file-lock move removed the false trapped-primitive edges — so these are real edges, not measurement artifacts. This makes the violation check a RATCHET: it cannot fail on what exists today, only on NEW undeclared edges. THREE entries were recorded debt, NOT intent. (1) shared-lib — PARTLY CLEARED 2026-08-10: audit-orchestration, model-eval, nav-audit and stores REMOVED from the grant (7 -> 3, confirmed against the observed graph after a full refresh). Method, per the preference order refactor > retag > declare: five top-level lib files were RETAGGED because they are feature coordinators whose LOCATION is fine and whose TAG was wrong (efficacy-lints/audit-shadow/finalize-outcomes/audit-arms -> audit-orchestration; model-ab-decision -> model-eval, adding no new edge since model-eval -> audit-orchestration was already declared and observed). config.mjs was NOT retagged — it is a genuine primitive, and its single feature import was a trapped vocabulary constant, so PREVIEW_GATE_MODES was REFACTORED out of lib/cycle/topology.mjs into lib/preview-gate-vocabulary.mjs (same move, same reason, as status-vocabulary.mjs), with topology re-exporting it so importers are unaffected. repo-inventory.mjs needed nothing; it imports only shared-lib. REMAINING (verified at source 2026-08-10, so the grant is a ratchet, not an endorsement): findings x5 (context/ledger/outcome-sync/suppression-policy reaching findings*.mjs — those three files are themselves lib-root and tagged findings by a specific rule, so this is the SAME retag-or-move question one layer down); claude-hooks x1 (repo-inventory -> quickfix-patterns for isSensitivePath, which duplicates the sensitive-paths.mjs primitive AGENTS.md calls the single source of truth); plan x1 (file-io -> plan-paths is a BACKWARD-COMPAT RE-EXPORT, not a use — file-io forwards it for 19+ importers, so this is a measurement artifact needing a migration, not a retag). (2) stores -> model-eval/persona-test — a LAYER INVERSION: the persistence layer reaching UP into feature domains. (3) cross-skill-bridge -> 11 domains — AGENTS.md calls this a thin facade; eleven deps is not thin. Do not grow these three without fixing the underlying coupling. ADDENDUM (tech-debt-backlog-triage, 2026-07-26): root-scripts -> install added — install.mjs/setup.mjs (repo-root entry points, caught by the *.mjs catch-all) import scripts/lib/install/prompt.mjs; same entry-point-to-implementation shape already declared for `scripts`, just never extended to the two root-level installers. Closes tech-debt topicIds 0fd83d0f/99f61113/a122a79b/d9f8c219.

_adjudication_2026_07_31_acceptance_back._context: Companion to _adjudication_2026_07_31 (which covers the layering pass). These three edges surfaced while clearing the unremediated-acceptance backlog: 11 [Architecture] findings across 6 runs. Two verdicts are POINTERS to decisions already taken — the decision existed, only the remediation_state write-back was missing, which is exactly why the pass kept re-raising them.
_adjudication_2026_07_31_acceptance_back.setup.mjs -> install: DECLARED 2026-07-26 — see the ADDENDUM in _comment_allowedDeps. Re-raised 5 more times because no remediation_state was written, so unremediated_acceptances kept listing it. Write-back done 2026-07-31 citing 3a2530ae. (The install.mjs half of this edge was instead RE-TAGGED by the layering pass — see L4 in _adjudication_2026_07_31 — so those 3 findings cite d1d8097c.) Tempted to move scripts/lib/install/prompt.mjs to shared-lib because it is a generic readline wrapper with no install-domain logic? That is a reasonable reading, but it second-guesses a call already taken on the entry-point-to-implementation shape. Reopen deliberately or not at all.
_adjudication_2026_07_31_acceptance_back.stores -> plan: NOT REPRODUCIBLE, CAUSE UNATTRIBUTED. plans-ship.mjs imports ../status-vocabulary.mjs, which resolves to shared-lib via scripts/lib/**, and stores -> shared-lib is allowed. Deliberately NOT written back as fixed: d1d8097c did not touch that file import lines, so the edge may have gone via a domain-map RETAG rather than a code change (the MAP ERROR class from 2026-07-20), and fix_commit_sha would be a misattribution. An unattributed disappearance is not evidence of a fix.
_adjudication_2026_07_31_acceptance_back.shared-lib -> audit-orchestration: RECORDED DEBT, NOT INTENT — must keep firing. config.mjs imports cycle/topology.mjs (PREVIEW_GATE_MODES) and efficacy-lints.mjs imports audit/glob-match.mjs; both real. _comment_allowedDeps entry (1) already names this as one of THREE debts with the fix stated (feature coordinators masquerading as domain-neutral primitives; retag or move them) and says not to grow them without fixing the coupling. DO NOT silence the recurring finding by adding an allowedDeps entry — converting a documented debt into a false declaration of intent is the one move this block exists to prevent.

_adjudication_2026_07_20._context: Four domain edges were reported by /audit-code's architecture pass in NINE consecutive rounds across two clusters (plan: sast-triage-routing). Adjudicated once, on the merits, so they stop consuming a finding slot every round.
_adjudication_2026_07_20.install -> plan: MAP ERROR, not a code defect. check-plan-status.mjs was swallowed by the scripts/check-*.mjs catch-all and tagged `install`. Fixed by a specific rule ahead of it; the edge is now plan -> plan (same-domain, always allowed). See that rule's _why.
_adjudication_2026_07_20.dashboard -> plan: INTENT — DECLARED. collect-reference.mjs calls parsePlanStatus to bucket plans by status. A dashboard is a read-model consumer by construction (it already draws on eight domains), so this is its established role, not erosion.
_adjudication_2026_07_20.brainstorm -> requirements: INTENT — DECLARED. policy-context.mjs's own docstring records this as a REUSE decision taken under the architectural-memory protocol rather than reimplementing ledger filtering. NOTE: declaring it CLOSES A CYCLE, because requirements -> brainstorm already exists. That is recorded as debt (4) rather than hidden by the declaration.
_adjudication_2026_07_20.supabase -> stores: FABRICATED, now FIXED IN CODE (2026-07-20). The edge came from `compat-bootstrap.sql` doing `CREATE SCHEMA auth; CREATE TABLE auth.users` (a parity shim for what Supabase provides natively), so every migration's `REFERENCES auth.users(id)` resolved to that file — a `supabase → stores` edge that reflects a PLATFORM dependency, not a real one on the shim. The earlier note said 'nothing to fix in code or map', but leaving it meant the mechanical adapter re-fabricated it every run and the bouncer kept hallucinating findings off it (32 accumulated). Fixed by `PLATFORM_SCHEMAS` in adapters/postgres.mjs: a reference to `auth.*` (and the other Supabase-managed schemas) is `proven-external`, like `pg_*`, so no local edge is created even when a shim defines a copy. Verified: runArchIntentAnalysis now reports 0 violations. Guard: tests/arch-intent-adapter-postgres.test.mjs.
_adjudication_2026_07_20._debt_4: requirements -> brainstorm exists only because requirements/{extract,gap-challenge}.mjs import callOpenAI from brainstorm/openai-adapter.mjs — a domain-NEUTRAL LLM primitive that happens to live inside the brainstorm domain. Same misplacement class as debt (1). Moving it to shared-lib breaks the cycle and touches ~5 real call sites; that is a mechanical module move deserving its own change and its own verification, not a rider on a map adjudication.

_comment_tests: tests is a VERIFICATION domain: allowed one-way into everything, with the inverse PROHIBITED — no production domain may import tests (enforced by the absence of `tests` from every other allowedDeps entry; a violation surfaces as an undeclared edge). This entry was UNVERIFIABLE until 2026-07-17: extract.mjs handed dep-cruiser a COMMON_SOURCE_DIRS allowlist with no `tests`, so the largest domain in the repo (380 files) produced zero observed edges while being fully symbol-indexed — the 12 entries here were hand-written from real knowledge but could never be corroborated. With `tests` cruised, all 12 proved real (zero over-declaration) and 17 more appeared. See docs/plans/observed-graph-discovery-unification.md — the allowlist remains a silent-blindness generator; this fixed the instance, not the class.
_comment_coverage: Observed-graph coverage contract (docs/plans/observed-graph-coverage-honesty.md 2.1.4). floor/attributionFloor are ratios in [0,1]; maxCruiseMs is the SOFT budget (degraded), hardTimeoutMs the parent-enforced kill. enforce:false ships first — arch:coverage-gate reports the verdict without failing for one cycle of real data. attributionFloor is deliberately low: an untagged domain is a domain-map gap, not a correctness bug; the load-bearing guard is the zero_attributed vacuity check, not this ratio.
_adjudication_2026_08_01: Layering pass L5 (docs/plans/dashboard-skills-index-layering.md). dashboard -> scripts REFACTORED AWAY, not declared — and the pre-existing declaration was REMOVED. scripts/lib/dashboard/collect-reference.mjs imported loadAllSkills from scripts/skills-help.mjs, a top-level CLI entry point; the two pure functions (parseSkill, loadAllSkills) moved verbatim to scripts/lib/skills-index.mjs (shared-lib), which dashboard already declares — so the fix added ZERO edges and deleted one grant. Why removal rather than accept-by-declaration: "scripts" was NOT an adjudication. It entered allowedDeps.dashboard on 2026-07-17 in the Phase-C baseline that set allowedDeps to the OBSERVED graph wholesale (see _comment_allowedDeps, which opens "BASELINE, NOT ENDORSEMENT"), which is AFTER the three findings it appeared to bless were raised (2026-07-15/15/16). Affirming it would have converted a mechanical snapshot into recorded intent the map explicitly disclaims. Same reasoning as the L4 RE-TAG decision in _adjudication_2026_07_31, and stronger here: skills-help.mjs was the SOLE producer of the edge (the only other ../../ import under scripts/lib/dashboard/** is audit-metrics.mjs, which tags audit-orchestration and is separately declared), so the grant covered exactly one import of one function while granting the whole current and future root-scripts domain. NO new rule was added: skills-index.mjs is a FILE, not a scripts/lib/<subsystem>/ directory, so it correctly falls through the scripts/lib/** -> shared-lib catch-all. Guards: tests/layering-contracts.test.mjs L5 (module resolves to shared-lib; the moved symbols are absent from BOTH skills-help.mjs's namespace and its __test__ object; "scripts" is absent from allowedDeps.dashboard — nothing else checks for a stale allowedDeps EDGE, since computeDeadIntent only finds dead DOMAINS) and tests/dashboard-collect-reference.test.mjs (first coverage of the consumer path). Closes tech-debt topicIds 7cd98d98/dafaf6c8/1f6dd42d.
_adjudication_2026_07_31: Layering pass (docs/plans/layering-and-mutation-contracts.md). L2 DECLARED: cross-skill-bridge -> model-eval. cross-skill.mjs is the CLI facade and already declares dispatch edges to arm-eval, audit-orchestration, nav-audit, persona-test and stores; model-eval was an omission in the intent layer, not a violation. L4 RE-TAGGED (not declared): install.mjs -> install. It was root-scripts only via the '*.mjs' catch-all, while its sibling scripts/install-skills.mjs was already 'install'. Declaring tests -> root-scripts would have granted every test module access to the whole current and future root-scripts domain to express one narrow relationship; re-tagging removes the edge instead. L1 and L3 were REFACTORED, not declared: CoverageSchema -> lib/coverage-schema.mjs and canonicaliseForHash -> lib/canonical-hash.mjs (both shared-lib), old exports removed.
_adjudication_2026_08_12: Layering pass (docs/plans/god-module-and-layering-debt.md). Baseline 14 violations / 9 domain edges at 581fea0b, measured by tests/arm-vocabulary-layering.test.mjs (derived, never a hand list). RETAGGED, not declared (preference order refactor > retag > declare): check-db-suite-enrolment.mjs -> scripts; lib/db/errors.mjs -> shared-lib; lib/audit-store-writers.mjs -> audit-orchestration; setup.mjs -> install. DECLARED, 2 grants: (a) scripts -> install — update-auditloop.mjs imports lib/install/deps.mjs, the entry-point-to-implementation shape already declared for root-scripts -> install on 2026-07-26 and never extended to this third installer. (b) tests -> cross-skill-bridge — a146bb7b moved scripts/lib/cross-skill/** into cross-skill-bridge on 2026-08-12 and did not re-baseline the INBOUND direction, so that domain's own four unit tests became violations overnight. `tests` already grants 29 of 32 domains; cross-skill-bridge was missing by timing, not by decision. NOTE this is NOT the shape _adjudication_2026_07_31 rejected: that refused tests -> root-scripts because root-scripts is the *.mjs catch-all, and the fix was to retag the file out of it — done here for setup.mjs. REFUSED: shared-lib -> stores. d5e66d35 removed `stores` from shared-lib's grant nine days ago (7 -> 3) and _comment_allowedDeps records it as debt; granting it back to clear three file edges would have reversed that and pre-authorised every future shared-lib -> stores import. Retagged the two files instead. The three group-C edges (audit-store-writers x2, durable-write -> db/errors) are DELIBERATE per audit-store-write-durability decisions 1b and 2c — argued and accepted there, re-raised every round since because nothing recorded the verdict. This is the record. ADDENDUM: retiring setup.mjs from root-scripts emptied that domain (install.mjs had already left in 2026-07-31), so root-scripts is REMOVED from allowedDeps + domainPurposes and its *.mjs/*.js catch-all rules now point at `scripts`. The rules are kept, not deleted — an untagged file is SKIPPED by analyseImports, so dropping the catch-all would hide every future repo-root script from the layering check.
